title: Linear cohomology sequence for a closed-immersion cokernel
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X,Y$ be $k$-schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-scheme-over-base], and let $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion over $k$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $\mathcal L,\mathcal E$ be sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules and $\mathcal M$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Define $(i_*\mathcal M)(U)=\mathcal M(i^{-1}U)$, with $\mathcal O_X$ acting through the structure-sheaf map. Use module cohomology as right derived global sections [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology], with the $k$-actions induced by the structure morphisms. There are canonical $k$-linear isomorphisms
$$c^q:H^q(X,i_*\mathcal M)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(Y,\mathcal M)\quad(q\geq0),$$
natural in $\mathcal M$, with $c^0$ the equality of global sections. For every short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal L\to\mathcal E\xrightarrow{u}i_*\mathcal M\to0$, the right-derived-global-sections long exact sequence, after these identifications, is an exact sequence of $k$-vector spaces
$$0\to H^0(X,\mathcal L)\to H^0(X,\mathcal E)\xrightarrow{c^0H^0(u)}H^0(Y,\mathcal M)\xrightarrow{\delta^0}H^1(X,\mathcal L)\to\cdots\to H^q(X,\mathcal E)\to H^q(Y,\mathcal M)\xrightarrow{\delta^q}H^{q+1}(X,\mathcal L)\to\cdots.$$
Here $\delta^q$ is the boundary of the specified module-sheaf sequence composed with $(c^q)^{-1}$. In particular, if $H^0(X,\mathcal L)=H^1(X,\mathcal L)=H^1(X,\mathcal E)=H^2(X,\mathcal E)=0$, then $c^0H^0(u)$ and $\delta^1:H^1(Y,\mathcal M)\to H^2(X,\mathcal L)$ are $k$-linear isomorphisms. No quasi-coherence, Noetherian, properness, or smoothness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Write $M_{ab}$ for the underlying abelian sheaf. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], the underlying map of $i$ is a closed embedding, and $(i_*M)_{ab}=i_*(M_{ab})$ sectionwise. Apply [lem-sc-zariski-module-abelian-cohomology-agree] on $X$ and $Y$, obtaining natural additive comparisons $a_X^q,a_Y^q$ normalized to the identity on sections. The normalized closed-pushforward delta-functor isomorphism $t^q:H^q(Y,M_{ab})\to H^q(X,i_*M_{ab})$ is supplied by [lem-sc-closed-pushforward-boundary-naturality]. Define $c^q=(a_Y^q)^{-1}(t^q)^{-1}a_X^q$. These are natural additive isomorphisms, and $c^0$ is the equality $(i_*M)(X)=M(Y)$.

proof.text: For $\lambda\in k$, let $\tau_M$ be multiplication by its image in $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$. Since $i$ is over $k$, $i_*\tau_M$ is multiplication by the image of $\lambda$ in $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ on $i_*M$: both act sectionwise by the same element of $\mathcal O_Y(i^{-1}U)$. Naturality from Step 1 gives $c^qH^q(X,i_*\tau_M)=H^q(Y,\tau_M)c^q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-scalar-endomorphism] on both schemes, this reads $c^q(\lambda x)=\lambda c^q(x)$. Thus $c^q$ and its inverse are $k$-linear.

proof.text: The module-sheaf category is abelian with enough injectives by [lem-sc-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. Global sections valued in $\operatorname{Mod}_{\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)}$ is additive and left exact: kernels are sectionwise by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and evaluation at $X$ preserves that kernel formula. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor] with this target module category to the specified short exact sequence. It gives the entire exact sequence starting in degree zero, with all maps module-linear and with its canonical derived connecting morphisms; these are the boundaries of [def-sc-module-cohomology-boundary]. Restrict their scalars along $k\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. This changes no underlying groups, kernels, or images, so the sequence stays exact and every map is $k$-linear.

proof.text: Replace each $H^q(X,i_*M)$ in Step 3 by $H^q(Y,M)$ using $c^q$. The incoming arrow becomes $c^qH^q(u)$ and the outgoing arrow becomes $\delta_X^q(c^q)^{-1}$, exactly the boundary specified in the statement. For adjacent maps $a,b$, an isomorphism $c$ carries $\operatorname{im}(a)$ to $\operatorname{im}(ca)$ and $\ker(b)$ to $\ker(bc^{-1})$; hence every exactness equality is preserved. Under the four vanishings the two relevant segments reduce to $0\to H^0(X,E)\to H^0(Y,M)\to0$ and $0\to H^1(Y,M)\xrightarrow{\delta^1}H^2(X,L)\to0$. Each middle map has zero kernel and full image, and is therefore a bijective $k$-linear map, hence a $k$-linear isomorphism.
